USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: The US should continue to escalate tariffs on Chinese goods, raising the rate on $200 billion of Chinese imports to 25% and preparing to impose tariffs on the remaining $300 billion of Chinese goods. This is the best opportunity in a generation to force China to change its unfair trade practices, intellectual property theft, and state-subsidized industrial policy. The US economy is strong enough to absorb short-term pain for long-term structural gain.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat score is -1.0 (clear opportunity) because China has backtracked on nearly all aspects of a draft trade deal (Reuters timeline, May 2019), demonstrating that only maximum pressure will yield results. The US has significant leverage: China's economy is more export-dependent on the US than vice versa, and the $419 billion trade deficit means the US has far more tariff ammunition remaining. Senator Graham's assessment that 'this is the best chance in my lifetime to get China to change their cheating ways' reflects bipartisan recognition of this leverage (Fox Business). The US stock market has recovered strongly in 2019 (Dow up 11% YTD per BBC), showing resilience to trade tensions. China's retaliatory tariffs on $110 billion of US goods are already near exhaustion, while the US can still target $300+ billion more. The collateral damage to US firms is real but manageable - as Brookings notes, 'this is not a big hit for the overall U.S. economy.' The action score is -1.0 (maximal escalation) because China's negotiating posture of backtracking on commitments demands a forceful response to restore credibility and maintain pressure. Holding or conceding now would signal weakness and embolden further Chinese intransigence.
key_factors: China backtracked on nearly all aspects of draft trade deal (Reuters, May 2019)

China's economy more export-dependent on US than vice versa
